title: Aloha Spirits brewery liquor license and zoning limits
summary: On November 12, the commission unanimously approved a small craft producer pub license for a brewery on South Kīhei Road. The license bars liquor made there from being taken off the property and sold elsewhere. In September, the commission accepted the application, but zoning questions arose over selling kegs or cases to stores, restaurants or bars, and no license could issue until zoning clearance was met.

timeline.text: The commission approved the brewery license in a unanimous roll call vote.
The motion for that license barred liquor made there from being taken off the property and sold elsewhere.
A brewery on South Kīhei Road applied for a small craft producer pub license.

New liquor license application number seven (Aloha Spirits Brewing and Distilling): The commission accepted the Aloha Spirits Brewing and Distilling application, with zoning among the requirements still to be met.
A motion to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion) about county liability failed, four to three.
Staff said zoning may not let a brewery pub applicant sell beer directly to wholesalers, restaurants or stores.
No liquor license will be issued to the brewery until it meets the zoning clearance requirement.
The applicant's attorney said zoning may not allow selling kegs or cases to stores, restaurants or bars.
The department is waiting for the planning department to confirm in writing what the brewery may do at its location.
Staff said the Planning Department raised new zoning questions about one applicant's planned uses.
